# lockfile

```go
import "github.com/lucasassuncao/movelooper/internal/lockfile"
```

Package lockfile provides exclusive, OS\-level advisory locks on a sidecar file, used to serialize work across movelooper processes.

The lock is held by the operating system for as long as the owning process holds the file open. It is released automatically when the process exits, including on a crash or a kill that runs no deferred code, so a lock can never be left stranded. That is the whole reason this package exists: an earlier PID\-file scheme had to guess whether the recorded process was still alive, and guessed wrong on Windows.

The lock file itself is deliberately never deleted. It carries no state — it is only a handle for the OS lock — and removing it would race with another process that has it open.

<a name="Lock"></a>
## type [Lock](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/movelooper/blob/main/internal/lockfile/lockfile.go#L28-L30>)

Lock is an acquired exclusive lock. Release must be called to free it, although process exit also releases it.

<a name="Acquire"></a>
### func [Acquire](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/movelooper/blob/main/internal/lockfile/lockfile.go#L34>)

```go
func Acquire(path string) (*Lock, error)
```

Acquire opens \(creating if needed\) the lock file at path and blocks until an exclusive lock is held. Parent directories are created as needed.

<a name="TryAcquire"></a>
### func [TryAcquire](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/movelooper/blob/main/internal/lockfile/lockfile.go#L40>)

```go
func TryAcquire(path string) (*Lock, error)
```

TryAcquire behaves like Acquire but never blocks: when another process already holds the lock it returns ErrLocked immediately.

<a name="Lock.Release"></a>
### func \(\*Lock\) [Release](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/movelooper/blob/main/internal/lockfile/lockfile.go#L64>)

```go
func (l *Lock) Release() error
```

Release unlocks and closes the underlying file. The lock file is left on disk on purpose; see the package comment.
